text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- International donors' conference for Bosnia scheduled for June 24 and 25 in Brussels will focus on aid which enables refugees to return to their homes, reconstruction of disputed town of Brcko and repairing infrastructure.

- Bosnia will chair a meeting of the Central European Intiative this week in Sarajevo devoted to the implementation of the Dayton peace treaty, Albania and the situation in Central European countries.

- U.S. embassy denies speculation that embassy staff members are being replaced because of heavy workload and says Washington regularly changes personnel every 12 months, especially in unstable regions.

- Establishing equal legal status of Serbs in the Moslem-Croat federation, and in Croatia as well, is unlikely without the same procedure being applied by Belgrade towards Moslems and Croats living in Yugoslavia, commentary says.

- The organisation and ethnic balance of the current diplomatic service cannot satisfy Bosnia's minimal needs as a state, says Jadranko Prlic, foreign affairs minister. Bosnia has no ambassadors in important countries such as Russia, Belgium and Britain, he says.

- Human Rights Coordination Centre of the office of the High Representative criticises recent judical appointments made in Sarajevo, saying that speedy manner in which the procedure was carried out and lack of criteria gives impression that the process was arbitrary. -- Reuters newsroom +387-71-663-864
